<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="ניסן_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518918187_theRebbe_312" batchId="meluket-_D7_A0_D7_99_D7_A1_D7_9F_meluket__BH_POST_1766518918187_theRebbe_312__p001">
  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section provides the header information for the maamar, including the Torah portion and date.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">With the help of Heaven.</t>
    <t s="1">Shabbos Parshas Vayikra,</t>
    <t s="2">Parshas HaChodesh,</t>
    <t s="3">Rosh Chodesh Nissan,</t>
    <t s="4">5731</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section notes that the maamar was delivered as a talk (hachna'ah).</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">(Talk)</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section discusses the distinction between solar years and lunar months, and questions why Nissan is called the head of the months of the year.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">"This month is for you the head of the months, it is the first for you of the months of the year."</t>
    <t s="1">Now,</t>
    <t s="2">the well-known statement of the Ibn Ezra is known:</t>
    <t s="3">"The moon has no year at all, just as the sun has no month at all."</t>
    <t s="4">That is,</t>
    <t s="5">the division of time called a year pertains to the sun,</t>
    <t s="6">for during a year the sun travels and revolves until it returns to its original place,</t>
    <t s="7">and then it revolves again once more, etc.,</t>
    <t s="8">therefore it is called "shanah," from the word "shinui" (change/repetition)</t>
    <t s="9">(that the same thing returns and is repeated once more),</t>
    <t s="10">but from month to month nothing changes in its course.</t>
    <t s="11">And the division of time called a month pertains to the moon,</t>
    <t s="12">for its course until it returns to the first point is the duration of a month,</t>
    <t s="13">but from year to year nothing changes in its course.</t>
    <t s="14">Based on this, we must understand what is written: "This month... for the months of the year,"</t>
    <t s="15">which mentions the matter of a year in relation to months.</t>
    <t s="16">Also, we must understand</t>
    <t s="17">what is written about Rosh Chodesh Nissan: "This month is for you the head of the months, it is the first...,"</t>
    <t s="18">yet the first of Tishrei is Rosh HaShanah.</t>
    <t s="19">And as explained in Likkutei Torah,</t>
    <t s="20">the precise meaning of "Rosh HaShanah"</t>
    <t s="21">(and not "beginning of the year"),</t>
    <t s="22">is that just as the head includes the life-force of all the limbs of the body,</t>
    <t s="23">so too Rosh HaShanah includes the life-force of the entire year,</t>
    <t s="24">for even though there is a renewal of life-force each day,</t>
    <t s="25">as the saying,</t>
    <t s="26">"Who renews in His goodness every day, constantly, the work of creation,"</t>
    <t s="27">and not only each day but even each moment,</t>
    <t s="28">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="29">there is an established order in the drawing down and renewal of life-force,</t>
    <t s="30">that first there is the drawing down of the general life-force on Rosh HaShanah,</t>
    <t s="31">and it is then divided into twelve heads of months,</t>
    <t s="32">and from Rosh Chodesh it is drawn to all the days of the month.</t>
    <t s="33">And it is explained at length and in more detail in Ateret Rosh,</t>
    <t s="34">that there are two aspects of "head,"</t>
    <t s="35">the first,</t>
    <t s="36">that the life-force of all the limbs of the body is first included in the head and from there is drawn to all the limbs,</t>
    <t s="37">and the second,</t>
    <t s="38">that even after the life-force has already been drawn to all the particular limbs, the head is their director,</t>
    <t s="39">and as explained in Tanya,</t>
    <t s="40">that even now</t>
    <t s="41">(after the drawing of life-force from the head to all the limbs)</t>
    <t s="42">the nourishment of the nails is drawn from the brain in the head,</t>
    <t s="43">and these two aspects also exist in Rosh HaShanah.</t>
    <t s="44">Based on this, we must understand what it means that Rosh Chodesh Nissan is "the head of the months, the first"</t>
    <t s="45">("first" also meaning "head")</t>
    <t s="46">"it is for you of the months of the year,"</t>
    <t s="47">that is,</t>
    <t s="48">that Rosh Chodesh Nissan is analogous to the aspects in the analogy of the head in its simple sense,</t>
    <t s="49">yet the aspect of Rosh HaShanah is on the first of Tishrei.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
